dicas.texto: Boa pergunta! Se duas frações representam a mesma parte do todo, elas devem ficar no mesmo ponto da reta numérica. O que isso significa sobre frações equivalentes?
Você está no caminho certo! Primeiro, divida a Linha 2 em 16 partes iguais (já que o denominador é 16). Depois, conte 12 dessas partes a partir do zero e marque o ponto.
Quase lá! Pense: 3/4 é o mesmo que quantos dezesseis avos? Tente multiplicar numerador e denominador por 4. Depois, veja se o ponto cai na mesma posição da Linha 1.
Você está muito perto! Divida a Linha 2 em 16 partes. Agora, comece do zero e conte: 1, 2, 3… até 12. Marque esse ponto. Ele coincide com o de 3/4? Se sim, use o sinal '='.
Se dois pontos estão exatamente na mesma posição na reta, o que isso diz sobre os números que eles representam?
Compare visualmente: olhe para o ponto marcado na Linha 1 (3/4) e veja se o ponto que você marcou na Linha 2 está alinhado verticalmente com ele.
Veja bem: 3/4 = ?/16. Multiplique 3 por 4… dá 12! Então 12/16 deve estar exatamente onde 3/4 está.
Confira: o ponto de 12/16 está logo abaixo do ponto de 3/4? Se sim, eles são iguais — então o sinal correto é '='.

Divide Line 2 into 16 equal parts by entering its denominator.
Mark the point for 12/16 on Line 2.
Compare the marked positions on Line 1 and Line 2.
Enter the numerator that completes the equivalent fraction ___/16.
Select the comparison sign between 3/4 and 12/16.
Complete the exercise after checking the fraction comparison.

erros.devolutiva: You used the denominator from the reference fraction. Line 2 must show the total number of parts in the target fraction 12/16, which is 16.
erros.buggyRule: Usar o denominador da fração de referência (3/4) em vez do alvo (12/16): denominador = {ref_den} = 4

erros.devolutiva: You multiplied 4 by 12, but the denominator is already given by the target fraction. Use the number below the fraction bar in 12/16.
erros.buggyRule: Multiplicar o denominador da referência pelo numerador alvo: 4 * 12 = 48

erros.devolutiva: You stopped at an intermediate denominator. To represent the target fraction, Line 2 must be divided into 16 equal parts.
erros.buggyRule: Multiplicar o denominador de referência por 2 (achando que 3/4 → 6/8 → 12/16, mas para no meio): usar 8

erros.devolutiva: You counted a boundary mark as an interval. Count the spaces between marks; twelve spaces from zero represent 12/16.
erros.buggyRule: Contar as marcas (ticks) em vez dos intervalos: posição = numerador + 1 = 12 + 1 = 13

erros.devolutiva: You counted zero as the first part. Zero is the starting point, so the first interval begins after zero.
erros.buggyRule: Contar começando do zero como primeira parte: posição = numerador - 1 = 12 - 1 = 11

erros.devolutiva: You reused the reference numerator instead of counting the requested intervals on Line 2. The target uses twelve of the sixteen intervals.
erros.buggyRule: Marcar a mesma posição visual da Linha 1, ignorando a nova escala da Linha 2

erros.devolutiva: Different denominators do not automatically mean different values. The two marks occupy the same position, so the fractions are equivalent.
erros.buggyRule: Assumir que frações com denominadores diferentes não podem ser iguais

erros.devolutiva: You entered the numerator from the reference fraction. The field asks for the numerator of the equivalent fraction whose denominator is 16.
erros.buggyRule: Responder com o numerador da fração de referência (3) em vez do alvo (12)

erros.devolutiva: You entered the denominator in the numerator field. The numerator is the number of selected parts, while 16 is already shown as the denominator.
erros.buggyRule: Digitar o denominador (16) no lugar do numerador

erros.devolutiva: The fractions have different forms, but their marks are at the same position. Choose the sign that means they have equal values.
erros.buggyRule: Concluir que as frações são diferentes porque a representação alvo foi digitada incorretamente (ex: 13/16 ≠ 3/4)

dicas.texto: Look at how many equal parts make the whole and how many parts are marked.
Read the marked parts as the numerator and the total equal parts as the denominator.
The reference line has four equal parts, and three of them are marked.
Record the fraction with the number of marked parts on top and the total number of parts below.
The denominator tells how many equal parts make the whole.
Find the denominator in the target fraction and enter that number in the Line 2 field.
Use the number below the fraction bar in 12/..., not the denominator from the reference fraction.
Enter the target denominator in the field, then confirm it so the line shows that many equal intervals.
On a number line, the numerator tells how many equal intervals to move from zero.
Start at zero, count the equal spaces, and stop after the number of spaces named by the numerator.
Line 2 has 16 intervals, so count spaces rather than vertical boundary marks.
Begin at zero, move one interval at a time, and stop after twelve intervals before confirming the point.
Equivalent fractions represent the same point on a number line.
Compare the locations of the two marks rather than comparing the denominators alone.
Check whether both marks lie at the same distance from zero.
If the two marks overlap at the same location, choose the relation that means the values are equal.
Equivalent fractions are made by multiplying the numerator and denominator by the same factor.
Find the factor that changes the denominator 4 into the denominator 16, then use that factor on the numerator.
The denominator changes from 4 to 16 by a factor of 4.
Multiply the numerator 3 by the same factor used to change 4 into 16, then enter that product.
The comparison sign should describe the relationship between the two values.
Use the number-line positions and the equivalent fraction you constructed to choose the sign.
The two marks are aligned, which means neither fraction is greater or smaller.
Choose the sign used when two fractions have the same value.
Before completing, make sure the fractions describe the same location on the number lines.
Review the denominator, marked point, numerator, and comparison sign in order.
Check that Line 2 uses sixteen parts, the numerator field represents the requested fraction, and the equality sign is selected.
When every displayed part is correct, use the completion control to submit the checked comparison.

exercicio.statement:
Are 3/4 and 12/16 equivalent? Mark 3/4 on Line 1 and 12/16 on Line 2 to find the answer.
Are they the same? Correct the equal sign.
